title: ByteSequenceV1
description: Proposed representation of one logical arbitrary finite byte sequence, with optional embedded bytes, external locations, digests, external content identifiers, or a fragmented storage representation. Storage representations describe ways to materialize the same logical byte sequence; byteLength and digests always describe the complete byte sequence represented by this object. This schema is not yet canonical.

byteLength.description: Length of the complete raw byte sequence represented by this object when known. Required when fragmented is present.

digests.description: Fingerprints computed directly over the complete raw byte sequence represented by this object.

algorithm.description: Digest algorithm identifier, for example sha-256.

value.description: Digest value encoded as lowercase hexadecimal unless the named algorithm specifies another representation.

identifiers.description: External content identifiers such as ni: or swh: URIs for the byte sequence represented by this object. These are distinct from raw-byte digests because an external identifier scheme may define its own framing or semantics.

data.description: The complete raw byte sequence represented by this object, embedded in the JSON document.

locations.description: URI-references from which the complete byte sequence represented by this object may be retrieved.

fragmented.description: A storage representation in which this logical byte sequence is assembled from positioned fragments. Semantically, the fragments must cover exactly the half-open interval [0, byteLength) with no gaps or overlaps, and each fragment's bytes must match the corresponding range of the whole sequence. JSON Schema validates the representation structure and required lengths; coverage, overlap, ordering-independent assembly, and digest equality require semantic/content validation.

fragments.description: Fragments of the logical byte sequence. Array order is not semantically significant; offset determines placement.
